proof.text:
Put $s=j'_!(1\otimes J't)$, so $v=s z_K$. Since the open tensor comparison of [def-exchange-projection] is natural in its ambient tensor variable, its naturality square at $t$ is
$$s\gamma_{j';AK,HFL}=c'(1\otimes t).$$
Postcompose the assumed open-factor identity by $s$. Substitution of this naturality equation and bifunctoriality of tensor give
$$vH(c)=c'(1\otimes t)(b\otimes1)\mu_{H;M,FL}=c'(b\otimes1)d.$$
Here $(1\otimes t)(b\otimes1)=(b\otimes1)(1\otimes t)$, with the intermediate objects determined by the displayed sources. This is the two-variable functor law, and the last equality is exactly the definition of $d$.

proof.text:
The exchange $e:GR\to R'H$ is a natural transformation [def-exchange-projection]. Its naturality at the single morphism $c:Q\to T$ reads
$$e_T\,G(R(c))=R'(H(c))e_Q.$$
Expand $G(\operatorname{PF}^c)$ using step 1, apply this equality, and use the functor law for $R'$ followed by step 2. The left side in the desired conclusion becomes
$$R'(v)e_TG(\operatorname{PF}^c)=R'(c')R'(b\otimes1)R'(d)e_QG(\pi_{p;M,L}).$$
Every equality here is either the displayed naturality square, preservation of composition, or substitution of the preceding step.

proof.text:
Apply the proper-factor identity assumed in the statement, exactly with $M=j_!K$ and $Q=M\otimes FL$ already fixed. It replaces the final three factors in step 3 by
$$R'(d)e_QG(\pi_{p;M,L})=\pi_{p';HM,GL}(e_M\otimes1)\mu_{G;RM,L}.$$
Consequently that expression is
$$R'(c')R'(b\otimes1)\pi_{p';HM,GL}(e_M\otimes1)\mu_{G;RM,L}.$$
This step is substitution of a hypothesis; it neither proves nor assumes any invertibility of $e$ or $\pi$.

proof.text:
The counit projection in [def-exchange-projection] is natural in its first variable. Apply its naturality square at $b:HM\to j'_!AK$, holding $GL$ fixed:
$$R'(b\otimes1)\pi_{p';HM,GL}=\pi_{p';j'_!AK,GL}(R'(b)\otimes1).$$
Insert this into step 4. Tensor functoriality gives $(R'(b)\otimes1)(e_M\otimes1)=(R'(b)e_M\otimes1)$. Replacing $b$ and $c'$ by their abbreviations now yields exactly
$$R'(\gamma_{j';AK,F'GL})\pi_{p';j'_!AK,GL}(R'(\beta_K)e_M\otimes1)\mu_{G;RM,L},$$
which is the required right side. No cancellation or inversion of an exchange or projection occurred.

title: Pasting the open and proper factors for compact-support projection/base change
statement:
Use a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] and its chosen-compactification maps [def-exchange-projection], at one coefficient stage with all displayed composites defined. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f=pj$ a compactification, and $h:\overline X'\to\overline X$, $a:X'\to X$, $p'$, $j'$ the pulled-back diagram. Set $F=Lp^*$, $F'=Lp'^*$, $G=Lg^*$, $H=Lh^*$, $A=La^*$, $J=Lj^*$, $J'=Lj'^*$, $R=Rp_*$, $R'=Rp'_*$. Let $\theta:F'G\cong HF$ be the canonical square comparison and $\sigma:A J\cong J'H$ the open square comparison. Write $e:GR\to R'H$ for proper exchange, $\pi$ for the proper counit projection, $\beta: Hj_!\to j'_!A$, $\gamma:j_!K\otimes P\to j_!(K\otimes JP)$ for the open tensor map, and $\mu$ for pullback-tensor comparison, with the coherent identifications of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Composition is right to left; all tensors are derived, completed at the integral stage.

For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ in these domains, set $M=j_!K$, $Q=M\otimes FL$,
$$d=(1\otimes\theta_L^{-1})\mu_{H;M,FL}:HQ\to HM\otimes F'GL,$$
$$z_K=j'_!\bigl((1\otimes\sigma_{FL})\mu_{A;K,JFL}\bigr)\beta_{K\otimes JFL},$$
The following hypotheses imply the pasted identity below:
$$z_K H(\gamma_{j;K,FL})=\gamma_{j';AK,HFL}(\beta_K\otimes1)\mu_{H;M,FL},$$
$$R'(d)e_Q G(\pi_{p;M,L})=\pi_{p';HM,GL}(e_M\otimes1)\mu_{G;RM,L}.$$
With target comparison
$$v=j'_!\bigl(1\otimes J'(\theta_L^{-1})\bigr)z_K$$
and $\operatorname{PF}^c=R(\gamma_j)\pi_p$, one has
$$R'(v)e_{j_!(K\otimes JFL)}G(\operatorname{PF}^c)
=R'(\gamma_{j';AK,F'GL})\pi_{p';j'_!AK,GL}(R'(\beta_K)e_M\otimes1)\mu_{G;RM,L}.$$
This is an identity of the specified compactification composites conditional on the two factor identities; no invertibility of proper exchange or projection is assumed. It is natural in maps of this diagram and is preserved by conjugation with natural compactification comparisons that intertwine its component maps.
